results.author: Maria Deutscher

Anyscale, the startup that Nscale has agreed to buy, was launched in 2019 by a group of computer scientists. It commercializes an open-source project called Ray that was created by its founding team. The software is used to optimize large-scale AI clusters.
...

Nscale, a British AI cloud company backed by Nvidia and Dell, announced on July 30, 2026 that it will acquire Anyscale, the commercial platform built around the Ray distributed computing framework, for approximately $1.65 billion. The deal vertically integrates Nscale's GPU infrastructure and data centre assets with the software tooling that enterprise machine learning teams use to run large-scale AI workloads. Anyscale's revenue grew 70% quarter-over-quarter prior to the acquisition. The open-source Ray framework remains community-governed under the PyTorch Foundation and is not part of the commercial transaction. The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2026.

results.title: A year ago, I sat down with the Anyscale team at Ray Summit. We talked about how we might contribute to Ray and build something together. Today, that conversation comes full circle – we've agreed to… | Daniel Bathurst | 47 comments
results.author: Daniel Bathurst
highlights:
A year ago, I sat down with the Anyscale team at Ray Summit. We talked about how we might contribute to Ray and build something together. Today, that conversation comes full circle – we've agreed to… | Daniel Bathurst | 47 comments
...
A year ago, I sat down with the Anyscale team at Ray Summit. We talked about how we might contribute to Ray and build something together. Today, that conversation comes full circle – we've agreed to acquire Anyscale. Yes, I know. Nscale, Anyscale. It's almost too on the nose, and I promise someone on our team has already made every joke there is to make about it. But honestly, the name is the least interesting part of this for me. At Nscale, we want to build a truly full-stack platform. One where an engineer can come to us for everything, from the power and the data center all the way through to actually running their AI workload, without stitching together five different vendors to get there. We built the infrastructure side first: land, power, data centers, orchestration. Anyscale enhances our software layer. Ray is the framework engineers reach for first when they need to run training or inference across thousands of GPUs, and now it can run natively on our stack. That's the bit I'm really excited about. Ray will remain open source, and Nscale is joining the PyTorch Foundation to support its long-term development, because we want to see it grow faster, not slower. Grateful to the Anyscale team for building something this good, and excited to have them join us. More on the deal via my interview in Bloomberg: https://lnkd.in/dzB9wSJa
